title: Michael DeBakey & Denton Cooley (1908–2008 / 1920–2016, 1963 Lasker) — Dacron, the Artificial Heart Betrayal, and the 38-Year War Across Fannin Street

teenKit.tldr: Michael DeBakey and Denton Cooley revolutionized heart surgery while fighting a bitter 38-year turf war across a single Houston street, culminating in a legendary medical betrayal involving the first total artificial heart.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Modern cardiovascular medicine exists because two hyper-ambitious geniuses pushed each other to achieve the impossible, proving that massive medical breakthroughs are often fueled by raw human ego and intense rivalry.
keyTakeaways: Michael DeBakey operated as an institutional emperor, building a massive medical empire through absolute discipline and systematic control.
Denton Cooley played the role of the virtuosic rebel, relying on blinding surgical speed and charm to bypass establishment rules.
The 1969 artificial heart implant detonated a decades-long feud when Cooley used a device developed in DeBakey's lab without permission.
